main_text.p: cū concretione illa, exemti non fuerint, edenti ovillos illes pedes confestim naufeam stomachiq; cruciatum excitabunt cum ructu & vomitione. Verisimile enim est venenosum quiddam subesse capillata huic congeriei, quod coctioni obsit. Vide Lemn. l. 3. cap. 5.[?] Caeterum aures suilla, rostrum, & pedes in summo honore mensarum sunt, hi tamen illo praestant, hoc vero cruribus. Vervecinos quidam aqua incoctos ex aceto mandunt, apio virente asperso. quandoq; frigunt, prunisq; torrent: bubalos elixos exacte quida frigunt: sed male, quia humiditatem nutrimentalem plane eliciunt.
Commendant etiam vitulinos elixos piperū & croci condimento addito: suilli craticula assantur, & ex cœpis concisis aceto q; aspersis sumuntur.
Aures suillas ex garo, veteres aceto q; & sinapi edendas voluerunt, vel ex garo oleoq; affuso vino. Hodie culina ganeaq; artifices pro varia praeparationis principatu certant.

Anserini pedes, omniumq; fere Planipedum, quod omittere nefas fere duxerim, succi suavitate, elixi praestant multis aliis, cumprimis vero in palati delitiis est membrana illa, quâ interveniente, vngues conjun-guntur.

page.notes: Printed "cap. s." after "l. 3." read as "cap. 5"; the numeral is doubtful. Tilde abbreviations (cū, perū, ganeaq;, stomachiq;) read as printed. The initial "Aures" carries a decorative mark and is treated as the start of a paragraph. The word "interveniente" and the final "guntur." sit in a larger, heavier type, which is taken as italic. No printed marginal notes are present.
